fields.flowNotes:
PitchRoll is an attendance and parent-communication app for cricket academies in Nagpur. The design language is clean and minimal with a dark green primary colour taken from the turf, Inter for all text, and 8pt spacing throughout. I built a small component library first - buttons, the player chip, the batch card - so everything stays consistent as I add features.

The app covers batch management, attendance marking, absentee messaging to parents, a monthly attendance report the academy owner can export, and a player profile with a photo. Attendance can be marked by tapping a player chip, which toggles between present, absent and late, and there is a bulk 'mark all present' for the days when everyone shows up, which the coaches told me is most Tuesdays.

The screen that carries the product is the attendance marking screen, because the coach has about thirty seconds between the boys arriving and the first drill, and if marking eighteen players takes longer than that he will go back to the paper register. Everything else in the app exists to make that thirty seconds possible or to make the data useful afterwards.

I made these in Figma because my handwriting is genuinely unreadable and I thought showing it properly would be better than showing a bad photo. Happy to redraw on paper if that is required.

notes: Return: the notes are a description of the product and its design system rather than a flow - no screen has a line saying what the user does and where it goes next - and nothing states an order, since the Figma frames carry no numbers and the notes never sequence them. The frames do cover arrival to attendance marked, one is an empty state, and the carrying screen is named with a reason, so those criteria hold. The reviewer should also quote the bar's line about screens generated by a tool rather than drawn, even though the scored failures are ordering and the written flow.
